Gramlot 0.2.16 adds the two declarative server round trips of the legacy pages: `remote`, the content of an element built by a `@source` method, and `dataRemote`, a Data value computed by an endpoint when it is read.

## What changes

- `remote`: the attribute `remote="<fragment>"` on an element, written by the node method `remote(name, **params)` in Python and `remote(name, params)` in JS, makes the element's content the fragment of the `@source` / `registerSource` method of that name. The call parameters are the attributes `remote_<k>` (with `^`/`=` pointers). The fragment is requested through `gramlot.src.remoteSource` at the element's start, again on every change of a `^` parameter and of the Data context; `_cachedRemote` skips equal parameters, `_if`/`_else` stop and cancel the request, `_onRemote` runs inline after the mount; a failure names the element. The `remote` attributes never reach the DOM.
- `dataRemote(destination_path, method, cacheTime=None, **params)`: a Data path that holds a resolver (`RpcResolver`, a `BagResolver` of genro-bag) calling the `@endpoint` `method` when the path is read and its cache has expired. `cacheTime` in seconds as in the legacy: `< 0` or `None` once, `0` at every read, `> 0` again after that many seconds. A read never waits: it returns the current value and starts the call; the answer is written with the Data event, so `^` consumers are projected; with `cacheTime: 0` the answer is written without the event (a value per explicit read, as the legacy's synchronous resolver). A `^` parameter change reloads at once; `_if` false removes the resolver and keeps the value; a failed load is thrown again naming the declaration.
- Both leave the exclusion lists of the builders (`remote`, `dataremote`). Out of 0.2.16, by decision: `lazy` loading by DOM visibility, `_waitingMessage`, the `tbody` merge, `sendInheritedAttributes`, `_resolved`, `_fired`, the alias `data(path, remote=…)`.
- Documents: GC-095 §105 (new), §015 and §085; GC-090; GC-210 exclusions row; constitution amendment 11.59.

## Upgrading from 0.2.15

- No protocol change: adapters are unchanged. Fragments are `@source` methods and values are `@endpoint` methods, as in 0.2.14.
- Pages: nothing to change; `remote` and `dataRemote` are additions.
